decision.summary: The hierarchy is documented but incomplete for release. Fable was a zero-weight technical non-response, GLM was invalid for crossing packet scope, and Kimi supplied the only valid substantive audit, assessing the Qwen process as warn with reliability 0.66. The Qwen records show material orientation sensitivity, including four critical repeated-raw-A mapped-winner flips and broader instability concentrated in 410m strata. The deterministic model gate correctly remains blocked; there is no scientific hard fail, no publication authorization, and no authorization for training signals or author email.

findings.issue: Mapped outcome flips from ppo to tie
findings.label: corrected-160m
findings.rationale: In ppo_first the reviewer says A continues with actions and B adds nothing, mapping to ppo. In sft_first the same pair is scored TIE/tie with both candidates called repetitive and incoherent. The standards applied are inconsistent across orientations.
findings.recommended_action: Re-score using a fixed rubric for repetition, coherence, and continuation so the tie boundary does not move with order.

audit.summary: Audited the Qwen records only, including the population summaries and all 20 selected pairs in both orientations. The two calibration pairs are mapped-winner consistent despite opposite raw winners, which is expected under swapped orientation. The main risk is among non-calibration pairs: 18 selected pairs are position-inconsistent, including several critical cases where raw A is chosen in both orientations while mapped_winner flips, and multiple tie-to-decisive changes after swapping. Because the sample was selected to over-represent inconsistencies, the failure rate should not be read as the population rate; however, the population still shows concentrated instability in 410m strata and a raw A skew among decisive reviews. Overall: warn, with re-adjudication recommended for critical orientation-sensitive pairs before any downstream use.
systemic_patterns: Calibration pairs are consistent: opposite raw A/B winners co-occur with the same mapped_winner, so the label-mapped logic can be correct when orientation is handled properly.

The selected sample is intentionally enriched for position-inconsistent records, but population summaries still show non-trivial inconsistency: corrected-410m 53/200 pairs, exact-410m 52/200, corrected-160m 39/200, corrected-70m 19/200, exact-70m 19/200, exact-160m 14/200.

Across non-calibration records, raw A choices exceed raw B choices among decisive reviews, most visibly corrected-410m A=203/B=150 and exact-410m A=185/B=128; this suggests a residual first-position/A preference in some strata.

Small-model 70m and 160m strata are tie-dominated in population summaries, and many selected inconsistencies are tie-to-decisive changes after orientation swaps rather than stable candidate preferences.

Several rationales are formulaic or under-specified, especially comparative statements without an explicit A/B subject, which weakens auditability even when the mapped winner is technically consistent.
No story prompts, candidate outputs, checkpoints, rewards, or training states were present in scope; findings are limited to Qwen reviewer-record process quality.
